sentences: The hypothesis \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\) would make existence of efficiently verifiable witnesses decidable in polynomial time.
This question asks whether that hypothesis also forces exact polynomial-time computation of every #P counting function.
The gap is that deciding whether a witness exists does not directly determine how many witnesses there are.
Resolving the implication would clarify how much additional power exact counting can retain after decision complexity collapses.
The source's standard uniform function-computation conventions must be preserved, and a method that enumerates all witnesses can still take exponential time despite a fast existence test.
